name: go9_capacity_breakthrough
hypothesis: Scale2000 proved more data at same architecture plateaus at 0.67. Three changes to break through: (1) 10 res blocks vs 6 — reference impl used 10 to reach 1-dan, (2) ownership head — winner at 500 iters, (3) cosine LR decay — constant LR may prevent fine-grained learning at low loss.
estimated_time: 20-28h (1000 iters × 100 games, 10 blocks ~40% slower than 6 blocks)
warm_start_note: 10-block network cannot warm-start from 6-block checkpoint. Must train from scratch. This is OK — the architecture change is the whole point.
success_criteria: Loss below 0.60 (breaking the 0.67 plateau). If 0% vs GnuGo at iter 500, the problem is deeper than capacity.

infra_requirements.gnugo: apt-get install -y gnugo. Eval at iter 250, 500, 750, 1000.
